safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 days to 1.84 days once explicit safety stock of 19,639 units is activated in ERP.

narrative: Material PL1__MF5A8C08 exhibits smooth, near-Normal daily demand averaging 10,411 units with a low coefficient of variation of 0.20, indicating a predictable and stable demand pattern over the observed period from March 2025 to March 2026. Lead times average 2.20 working days with moderate variability (CV=0.51), contributing meaningfully to safety stock requirements. The current SAP safety stock of zero provides no buffer against demand or lead-time fluctuations, making stockouts highly probable; the recommended (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 19,639 units addresses this gap and achieves the 95% service level target within the available storage capacity of 149,768 units.
warnings: SAP safety stock is currently 0 — no buffer against lead-time or demand variability. Immediate risk of stockouts.
4 demand outliers detected and winsorised (IQR method) prior to parameter estimation.
Storage capacity utilised at 89.2% post-replenishment; monitor for capacity pressure if demand increases.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous Review Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth near-Normal demand with stable high-volume throughput (~10,400 units/day) is ideally served by a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The EOQ formula yields a well-defined economic order quantity far above the MOQ constraint (113,893 >> 3,421), and the near-Normal distribution of demand over lead time makes the z-score safety stock formula directly applicable without distribution fitting.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is 89.2% utilised at the peak post-replenishment inventory level (safety stock + order quantity = 133,532 units vs. 149,768 limit). A demand surge requiring higher safety stock or a MOQ increase could breach the storage ceiling. Recommend reviewing warehouse allocation if demand grows by more than 12%.
